chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When there are three people, two of them should not whisper privately to each other to the exclusion of their companion, for in that is something that saddens and hurts him.

key_terms.يَتَنَاجَى: to whisper privately or converse secretly

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette regarding whispering among three people?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'ghibah al-jalilah' (overt exclusion) as a social sin, emphasizing that private conversation among a trio creates an emotional barrier for the third party. Scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Tusi highlight this as a practical application of adab (etiquette) to preserve communal harmony and prevent the psychological harm of feeling marginalized. It serves as a foundational rule for group dynamics, ensuring that no individual is left in a state of uncertainty or hurt due to exclusive whispering.
